evidence: The films were characterized by a number of surface sensitive analysis techniques, by X-ray diffraction and by optical absorption. The crystallographic structure was studied by X-ray diffraction and LEED, and the surface morphology by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The composition and electronic structures of the films were studied by means of AES, XPS, UPS and optical absorption. The surface morphology was studied by SEM. The absorption edge of the films was measured optically. The electronic structure of the films can be probed by angle-resolved UV photoemission spectroscopy (UPS). The films were found to be clean, smooth and featureless, and they crystallized with a preferential orientation in the (111) direction. The electronic structure of the films exhibited characteristic features of the bulk material, as deduced from the angle-resolved photoemission and optical absorption. The size of coherent areas (particles) in films grown by ALE were calculated from the full width at half maximum (FWHM) of the (111) peak as a function of the growth temperature. The surface morphology was studied by SEM. The growth of the films was accomplished by up to 104 sequential alternate monolayer deposits of zinc and tellurium onto pieces of rectangular microscope soda lime glass of dimensions 0.2 mm x 8 mm x 10 mm. The film thickness was determined by the interference colours of the film or by a mechanical stylus tip technique. The surface morphology was studied by SEM.
